# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems (legacy "BILL-OLD" and new "BILL-NEW") will run concurrently in parallel-write/dual-reconciliation mode throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches by cohort; the old system remains fully operational as a fallback until well after the last user batch has been verified stable. No decommissioning work occurs until a separate, later phase outside this migration's user-facing scope.

---

## Phase 1 — Pilot (Internal + Opt-In Canary)

**Population:** 1% of users (~400 accounts) — internal test accounts, employees, and opt-in low-risk customers (no active disputes, no complex proration/multi-subscription setups).

**Entry criterion:** BILL-NEW has passed full parallel-run validation in staging for 14 consecutive days with zero critical invoicing discrepancies; rollback tooling (single-account revert to BILL-OLD) has been tested successfully end-to-end at least 3 times.

**Goals:** Validate data migration accuracy, dual-write reconciliation, and rollback mechanics under real (low-stakes) traffic.

**Exit criterion:** Invoice/charge parity between systems ≥99.95% for the full pilot cohort over 7 consecutive days, and no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents open.

---

## Phase 2 — Expanded Cohort (Graduated Ramp)

**Population:** 25% of users (~10,000 accounts) — introduced in three sub-waves (5% → 15% → 25% cumulative), segmented to exclude highest-ARR enterprise accounts and users on legacy/custom contract terms.

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by Billing Eng, Finance, and Support leads; support ticket volume attributable to billing migration in Phase 1 is below the halt threshold (see Metrics/Halt Conditions below) for the full 7-day observation window.

**Goals:** Stress-test at meaningful volume, validate dunning/retry logic, payment gateway routing, tax calculation, and customer-facing statements at scale.

**Exit criterion:** Payment success rate for migrated cohort within 0.5 percentage points of BILL-OLD baseline; reconciliation discrepancy rate ≤0.05% sustained for 7 consecutive days; each sub-wave individually meets this bar before advancing to the next sub-wave.

---

## Phase 3 — General Availability Rollout

**Population:** 74% of users (~29,600 accounts) — all remaining standard accounts, migrated in weekly batches of no more than 15% of total user base per batch, sequenced by account complexity (simplest billing profiles first, enterprise/custom-contract accounts last).

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; on-call and support teams have completed migration-specific training; automated per-account rollback tooling is confirmed capable of reverting a full batch (not just single accounts) within 4 hours if needed.

**Exit criterion (= end of user migration):** 100% of the 40,000 users successfully migrated with reconciliation discrepancy rate ≤0.05% sustained for 14 consecutive days, and no open Sev-1/Sev-2 billing incidents.

> **Important boundary:** Phase 3 covers migration of the final batch of users only. Any decommissioning, disabling, or deletion of BILL-OLD is explicitly out of scope for Phase 3 and will not begin until a separate Phase 4 ("Legacy Decommission") starts no earlier than 30 days after Phase 3's exit criteria are met, with its own independent entry criteria (full historical data archival verified, finance audit sign-off, and zero reliance on BILL-OLD for active billing, reporting, or support workflows).

---

## Metrics and Halt Conditions

Rollout is automatically paused (no further batches advanced) and escalated to the migration steering group if any of the following occur:

- **Reconciliation discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5%** of migrated accounts' invoices/charges in any rolling 24-hour window (primary halt trigger).
- Failed payment rate for migrated cohort rises more than 2 percentage points above the BILL-OLD baseline for the equivalent cohort, sustained over 24 hours.
- Billing-related support ticket volume for the migrated cohort exceeds 3x the pre-migration baseline rate in any 48-hour window.

A halt freezes further migration batches but does not automatically roll back already-migrated users; rollback of a batch is a separate decision made by the steering group based on root-cause severity.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missing charges during dual-write window due to reconciliation logic bugs | Run automated reconciliation diffing every 15 minutes with alerting, and require 7+ days of clean parallel-run data before advancing any phase | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Payment gateway or tax-calculation vendor behaves differently under BILL-NEW, causing declined transactions | Run shadow-mode transactions against BILL-NEW without settling funds before each phase, and maintain a tested one-click batch rollback to BILL-OLD | Payments Platform Lead
RISK: Customer confusion or trust erosion from unexpected invoice formatting/timing changes | Pre-notify affected users by email at least 7 days before their batch migrates, and staff Support with migration-specific FAQ and escalation path | Customer Support Lead
RISK: Enterprise accounts with custom contract terms are mismapped, causing revenue leakage or overbilling | Require manual Finance review and sign-off for every custom-contract account before inclusion in Phase 3, with dedicated migration runbooks per contract type | Finance Operations Lead
RISK: Migration batches proceed faster than support/on-call capacity can absorb incident load | Cap batch size at 15% of total users per week and require on-call headcount confirmation as a go/no-go gate before each batch | Program Manager

PHASES: 3
